about: Surviving Stryker mutants individually justified as equivalent (no input changes any observable result) or unreachable, ONE ENTRY PER MUTATION SITE. Checked by tools/pca-audit/stryker/check-equivalents.mjs. Keyed by package, file, mutator, original text, replacement, trimmed source line and occurrence (which copy of that line text in the file); lineno is a hint only and multiplicity covers the same mutant reported more than once on one line.
also_audited_note: Packages in the Stryker plan (.github/scripts/ts-stryker-plan.mjs) that have no equivalent-mutant entries yet: their survivors must be killed by tests or listed here with a reason; the merge job fails on an unlisted survivor. A package with entries is in the plan by that alone.

The linear-time parser admits only: literals, `.`, classes whose ranges it checks are ordered, the escapes d D w W s S t n v f r 0 xHH uHHHH cX and escaped punctuation (no octal, backreference, \k, \p, \b, \B), balanced (...) and (?:...) groups, `|`, quantifiers * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} with m >= n and at most one lazy `?`, never on an assertion or another quantifier, and ^ $. Each of these is also a production of the ECMAScript (Annex B, no u/v flag) pattern grammar, and none of the early errors V8 raises (out-of-order range or quantifier, invalid group name, dangling group, quantified lookaround, invalid escape) can arise from them; wrapping in ^(?: )$ keeps the group balanced because the parser required src itself to be balanced. Checked differentially, not only argued: src/regex-guard-compiles.test.ts asserts guard-accepts implies new RegExp compiles over 300k seeded token-grammar sources and the edge list (6M run once, no counterexample).

Cost cap only: no valid consistency proof for sizes < 2^53 needs more than 2*53+1 = 107 path nodes, and every surplus node is rejected by the algorithm (sn reaches 0 -> 'if (sn === 0n) return false'; size 0 and equal sizes require an empty path). Removing the cap changes work, not the verdict.

equivalents.line: if (!diffs.every((d) => verifyShadowDiff(d, log.signer) && d.shadow_digest === o.shadow_digest && d.enforced_digest === o.enforced_digest) || diffs.length !== s.diverged) return no('bad_diff', 'a recorded diff does not verify, belongs to another pair, or is missing');
equivalents.reason: Every diff comes from log.diffs(o.shadow_digest), which is keyed by the outcome digest stored in the diff's own shadow_digest field; changing that field after the fact breaks the signature that verifyShadowDiff checks first, so the equality is always true when the operand is reached.

equivalents.line: for (const e of o.explanations ?? []) if (verifyExplanation(e) && o.principals.includes(e.principal) && e.shadow_digest === o.shadow_digest) explained.add(e.action_digest);
equivalents.reason: A non-object placeholder entry makes verifyExplanation return false (isObj fails), so it never adds to the explained set, exactly like an empty list.

equivalents.line: if (!(enforced.shadow ?? []).includes(digest)) throw new RangeError('promoteShadow: the candidate is not listed in the enforced revision\'s shadow');
equivalents.reason: enforced.shadow ?? [] is only searched with includes(digest) where digest is a bundle digest; a fallback list holding another string never contains it, same as the empty list.
